key_insight: A transverse-field Ising model with a global, non-monotonic time-dependent field can simulate arbitrary quantum circuits with only polynomial overhead, making it polynomially equivalent to gate-model quantum computation.
engineering_relevance: This connects widely studied analog Ising hardware and quantum annealing-style platforms to universal quantum computation, while also implying limits on efficient classical simulation of such dynamics.
method: Builds on global-control techniques from recent Rydberg-atom results.
Constructs a simulation mapping from arbitrary circuits to the Ising model with a time-dependent global transverse field.
Proves polynomial overhead in time, number of qubits, and energy scale.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical construction and polynomial-overhead proof rather than an experimental benchmark or numerical dataset.
watch_item: The overheads are stated to be large, so practical implementation on real hardware may be inefficient despite the universality result.
paper_title: Polynomial equivalence of the global transverse-field Ising model and the gate model of quantum computation
